title: Wandering Aengus
html_source: First referenced by Buck Mulligan in Episode 9, Scylla and Charybdis, “Come, Kinch. Come, wandering Aengus of the birds,” (1093). Aeungus, son of Dagda, was the Irish god of youth, beauty, and love. He is portrayed with the birds of inspiration hovering about his head. Continually in search of his ideal mate, who had appeared to him in a dream, in some versions of the legend he discovers her as a swan, transforms himself into a swan, and flies away with her.
